content: 1. Context is critical when designing interventions to prevent child marriage; a one-size-fits-all approach is not effective. 2. WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of preventing early pregnancy and improving reproductive health outcomes among adolescents in developing countries. 3. Administering deworming treatments to pregnant women has been shown to positively impact child survival and health outcomes. 4. WHO recommendations on health promotion interventions for maternal and newborn health provide evidence-based strategies to improve outcomes. 5. WHO guidelines on antenatal care aim to ensure a positive pregnancy experience for women through comprehensive and individualized care. 6. Postnatal care recommendations from WHO focus on enhancing maternal and newborn health to ensure a positive postnatal experience. 7. Education on contraceptive use for women after childbirth is essential for family planning and reproductive health, as highlighted in Cochrane reviews. 8. The Immunization Agenda 2030 outlines a global strategy to ensure equitable access to vaccines, leaving no one behind. 9. The framework for reopening schools, developed by UNICEF, provides guidance on safely resuming education during crises. 10. WHO’s interim statement on COVID-19 vaccination for children and adolescents addresses the importance of immunization in this age group. 11. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis management in children and adolescents offers detailed protocols for effective care. 12. Interventions targeting high-burden infectious diseases in children and adolescents, as analyzed in meta-analyses, demonstrate significant health benefits. 13. Air pollution poses age-dependent health risks, particularly for children in lowand middle-income countries, as shown in modeling studies. 14. Handwashing promotion programs in schools have been proven to reduce disease transmission, as evidenced by randomized controlled trials. 15. Global studies on handwashing practices among adolescents highlight the need for improved hygiene education and infrastructure. 16. The roadmap to defeat meningitis by 2030 outlines strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of this life-threatening disease. 17. Outcomes of meningococcal disease in adolescents underscore the importance of early diagnosis and comprehensive care. 18. WHO’s roadmap to end tuberculosis in children and adolescents emphasizes the need for targeted interventions and global collaboration. 19. Cancer control strategies, including early detection, palliative care, and prevention, are critical for reducing the global cancer burden. 20. Digital health interventions for adolescent and young adult cancer survivors show promise in improving long-term outcomes. 21. Exercise and motor interventions during and after treatment for acute lymphoblastic leukemia in children improve physical activity and motor outcomes. 22. WHO’s package of essential noncommunicable disease interventions for primary health care provides a framework for addressing chronic conditions. 23. Chronic skin diseases in adolescence require specialized services to address their physical and psychological impact. 24. WHO’s pictorial training guide helps recognize neglected skin diseases, improving diagnosis and management in underserved areas. 25. Patient education in chronic skin diseases is essential for improving self-management and treatment adherence. 26. The IMAI district clinician manual provides comprehensive guidance on hospital care for adolescents and adults. 27. WHO’s position paper on human papillomavirus vaccines highlights their role in preventing cervical cancer and other HPV-related diseases. 28. Eye care integration into health systems is essential for addressing preventable blindness and visual impairment. 29. WHO standards for safe listening devices aim to prevent hearing loss caused by exposure to high sound levels. 30. Suicide prevention strategies, as outlined in WHO’s implementation guide, focus on reducing risk factors and promoting mental health. 31. Addressing adolescent nutrition gaps is critical for advancing public health and achieving sustainable development goals. 32. WHO guidelines on sugar, potassium, and sodium intake provide evidence-based recommendations for improving dietary habits. 33. Iron and folic acid supplementation for adolescent girls and women is vital for preventing anemia and associated health issues. 34. Management of severe malnutrition in children requires specialized protocols to ensure effective treatment and recovery. 35. Comprehensive sexuality education is essential for empowering young people and promoting informed decision-making about their health. 36. WHO’s global standards for health-promoting schools emphasize the importance of integrating health education into the school curriculum. 37. Rapid assessments of adolescent health programs in South-East Asia highlight the need for targeted interventions and policy development. 38. Lessons from the Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) guidance demonstrate the importance of context-specific approaches. 39. Addressing the global burden of disease among children and adolescents requires coordinated efforts and evidence-based strategies. 40. WHO’s health systems strengthening glossary provides a comprehensive resource for understanding key concepts in health system development.
